title: Service
hook: practice turned outward: time given to others
tomorrow: who washed the sick monk nobody would touch?

segments.voice: Yesterday, your inner teacher: know for yourself, by the light the teaching gives. Today that light turns outward.

Put your own oxygen mask on first: anyone who's flown has heard it. Mai's summer program has a community art day this weekend, painting a mural at a youth center, and she almost skipped the sign-up. Her reason: she can barely sit through the chanting without fidgeting, so who is she to help anyone? Inside the Buddhist texts, both sides of her argument have a voice.
screen: `YOUR OWN MASK FIRST.` → `A MURAL AT A YOUTH CENTER.` → `"WHO AM I TO HELP?"`

segments.voice: The first voice is in the Dhammapada: let each person first set himself in what is right, and only then teach others; that way the wise won't come to grief. Its case is real. Help from someone who hasn't tamed their own anger can do harm, and you can't give what you don't have. The second voice is in the Vinaya. Soon after his awakening, the Buddha sends his first disciples out to wander for the good of the many, for the happiness of the many, out of compassion for the world. Its case is real too. The world won't wait for anyone to be finished, and those disciples were sent out while they were still new. Both are scripture, and Buddhists hold them together in their own ways. In the Mahayana schools, including the Vietnamese temples of Mai's family, the ideal is the bodhisattva, who vows to keep working for the freedom of all beings. In Theravada lands, monks walk for alms each morning and lay people serve by feeding them, and both the giving and the receiving count as practice. Either way, service isn't an extra after the real work. It's practice turned outward: time and hands given to others, while the training goes on.
screen: `FIRST, SET YOURSELF RIGHT.` · `GO, FOR THE GOOD OF THE MANY.` · `THE BODHISATTVA'S VOW; THE ALMS ROUND.` · `PRACTICE TURNED OUTWARD.` · then, large: `OUTWARD.`

segments.voice: Count on your fingers the people whose service you used today without thinking: whoever grew your breakfast, drove the bus, cleaned the floor, answered a question. One finger for each. Then rest your hands in your lap and stay with them while the sit runs.
Service: practice turned outward, your time and hands given to others while your own training goes on.
Your line: outward. Nobody in the Vinaya waited to be finished first. Twenty-one days into the block.

howItsDone: Buddhists serve through temple work, feeding monks on their alms rounds, and volunteering in their wider communities; in Mahayana traditions the bodhisattva vow to work for the freedom of all beings frames service as part of the path.

Dhammapada.meaning: a collection of the Buddha's sayings in verse

Vinaya.meaning: the book of discipline for Buddhist monks and nuns

Mahayana.meaning: Buddhist schools found in East Asia and Vietnam, among others

bodhisattva.meaning: one who vows to work for the awakening of all beings

Theravada.meaning: the Buddhist school of Sri Lanka and mainland Southeast Asia

sources.ref: Vinaya Pitaka, Mahavagga I.11.1 (the disciples sent out to wander)

notes: Dhammapada 158 paraphrased (Max Müller's wording is close: 'Let each man direct himself first to what is proper, then let him teach others; thus a wise man will not suffer'; not quoted because the exact wording wasn't certain).

Vinaya Mahavagga I.11.1 paraphrased ('for the good of the many, for the happiness of the many, out of compassion for the world'); the number of disciples sent is left out on purpose. 'While they were still new' is a reading of the setting (soon after the first disciples' awakening); confirm.

Descriptions of Mahayana (bodhisattva vow) and Theravada (alms round; giving and receiving as practice) are general and say who holds what without ranking. Gloss for Mahayana/Theravada geography is general; confirm wording.
Shape: debate (two voices inside the texts; the fork asks for the 'fix yourself first' view's best case). Mai's storyline: her program's community art day, a mural at a youth center.
Surprising fact: the Buddha sent his first disciples out to teach soon after they awoke, not after long training.
